title: Redwood discovery - SolacePay latency & throughput
summary: Discovery for latency and throughput requirements across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. SolacePay wants p95 <= 200ms for short inference, burst concurrency ~200, streaming support and 500-800 tokens/sec target for typical prompt patterns. Discussed benchmarking plan, SOC2/KMS concerns, and next steps for PoC and pricing.
next_steps: Jamie to send high-level pricing and Dedicated sizing options (by 2026-07-23)
Sofia to share benchmark script, perf runbook, and sample Postman collection (by 2026-07-24)
SolacePay (Mike) to share sample prompts and qps distribution + p95 target confirmations (by 2026-07-28)
Schedule 1-hour deep technical benchmark run with SolacePay (week of 2026-07-27)
action_items: Jamie Park: Send pricing + high level Dedicated config (2026-07-23)
Sofia Martinez: Share benchmark repo, scripts, and runbook (2026-07-24)
Mike Chen: Provide sample workload, typical prompt lengths, and desired p95 targets (2026-07-28)
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE on this account. Sofia from our solutions team is here too. How are you folks?
[00:06] Daniel Ortiz: Good, thanks. We're excited to dig in
short on time so we'll focus on latency/throughput.
[00:10] Mike Chen: Yeah hi, Mike here. Head of ML at SolacePay. Our primary question is hosted vs dedicated vs private 
 what hits our p95 SLA and how do we benchmark token/sec.
[00:18] Jamie Park: Perfect. Sofia, you want to do a quick framing?
[00:21] Sofia Martinez: Sure. Quick agenda: current stack, latency targets (p95), concurrency, streaming needs, and benchmarking plan. We'll cover trade offs 
 batching, quantization, KV cache, and private/VPC considerations.
[00:31] Priya Rao: Sounds good. Quick context: we're building real-time fraud detection snippets and chat flows inside the payments app. Typical prompt lengths are 40-120 tokens, sometimes up to 400 for extended context. We need p95 sub-200ms for short flows, and sustained throughput during peak periods 
 about 150-250 concurrent requests.
[00:46] Sofia Martinez: Gotcha. When you say p95 200ms, is that end-to-end from client to response or model inference only?
[00:52] Mike Chen: End-to-end 
 that's what product measures. We can tolerate slightly higher for long streaming outputs, but for short decisions we want perceptible snappiness.
[01:00] Jamie Park: Good flag. Hosted can often meet low-latency p95s for small models and short sequences, thanks to warm pools and our autoscaling, but Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency under higher concurrency. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds more network variability depending on customer infra.
[01:16] Daniel Ortiz: What about streaming? We have streaming for progressive scoring in the UI, so partial token streaming is important.
[01:22] Sofia Martinez: We support streaming on Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports it too but you need to ensure networking and egress rules allow the persistent streams. Streaming affects tokens/sec metrics because you surface tokens as they're generated 
 effective token/sec is often lower when you include client-side handling.
[01:36] [00:38] Mike Chen: Can you explain p95 sources 
 is that model compute or queuing?
[01:40] Sofia Martinez: It's both. p95 includes model compute time per token, KV cache hits/misses, batching delays (if you enable dynamic batching), and queuing during concurrency spikes. On Dedicated you can tune batching policies and capacity to reduce queuing.
[01:52] [00:44] Priya Rao: We're also considering quantized models to save cost. How does that affect latency?
[01:55] Sofia Martinez: Quantization typically reduces memory and improves throughput; for many models 4-bit quantization has minimal latency impact and can even reduce latency for memory-bound workloads. But some kernels may be slower on specific GPU types; we'll validate in the benchmark.
[02:08] Jamie Park: For your numbers 
 short prompts 40-120 tokens, concurrency 150-250 
 I'd recommend a Dedicated pool initially to hit predictable p95 targets and run a controlled benchmark.
[02:18] Daniel Ortiz: What's the realistic tokens/sec we should expect for our typical prompt? We want to estimate cost.
[02:22] Sofia Martinez: Depends on model size and GPU type; e.g., 13B on A100 has very different tokens/sec than 70B on H100. Rough ballpark: with batch size tuned and no KV cache, you might see 300-800 tokens/sec for mid-size models; bigger models or longer contexts will drop. We'll provide more precise numbers in the benchmark.
[02:39] [00:50] Mike Chen: And p95 200ms for a 40-120 token prompt 
 is that feasible?
[02:44] Sofia Martinez: For short generations and efficient models, yes on Dedicated and on Hosted with reserved capacity. But if you're doing full-context 400-token outputs it will be higher. Also, streaming handshake and network RTT add to end-to-end.
[02:56] Jamie Park: Also want to call out prefix/KV cache 
 if you use KV cache for static system prompts or user context, your per-request compute drops a lot for subsequent requests. That helps p95 a lot for conversational flows.
[03:10] Priya Rao: Our flows mix fresh context and repeated prompts; cache hit rate might be 60-70% depending on session.
[03:15] Sofia Martinez: That will materially help. We'll include KV cache enabled scenarios in the perf script.
[03:20] [00:57] Daniel Ortiz: On security 
 SOC 2 and KMS 
 if we go Dedicated or Private, what's available?
[03:26] Jamie Park: Hosted is SOC 2 + SSO support; Dedicated includes VPC peering options and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; Private gives you full control and optional on-prem deployment. We'll attach our security pack.
[03:36] [01:01] Mike Chen: Great. For benchmarking, we'd like to run p95 latency at varying concurrencies: 50, 150, 250, and see the breakdown tokenization, model compute, batching delay, queuing.
[03:47] Sofia Martinez: That's exactly what we normally do. We'll share a benchmark repo with a load generator that reports p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, model latency, and queuing metrics. It uses synthetic prompt distribution you can replace with your real sample.
[03:59] Jamie Park: We'll also include a 'streaming' mode where we measure time-to-first-token and tokens-per-second for burst responses.
[04:08] [01:13] Priya Rao: About costs 
 if we need Dedicated, how do we size? Do we buy GPUs or vCPU equivalents?
[04:13] Jamie Park: We size Dedicated by expected sustained RPS and desired headroom for burst. We'll propose a configuration (e.g., N H100s for model X or mix of M60/A100 depending on availability). Pricing is monthly reserved capacity plus usage for overages; I'll send a sample calc.
[04:25] Mike Chen: Can we do a short smoke perf test on Hosted first to baseline?
[04:28] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we'll set up a hosted benchmark 
 it's the fastest to get running. But for Warranty on p95 under heavy concurrency you'll want Dedicated. Hosted is great for early validation.
[04:38] [01:33] Daniel Ortiz: Any gotchas with autoscaling for concurrency? We worry bursts might still hit tail latency.
[04:44] Sofia Martinez: Autoscaling has cold-starts; we recommend a warm pool and burst capacity policy; Dedicated avoids most of this because it's reserved hardware. We can set circuit-breaker fallbacks to a cheaper model for high load to keep availability.
[04:57] Jamie Park: Another tip: tune continuous batching window 
 shorter window reduces latency but lowers throughput; we can recommend policies based on your traffic shape.
[05:07] Priya Rao: Ok makes sense. Mike, do you have any strict compliance on data residency?
[05:11] Mike Chen: We need EU data residency for European customers; most infra is in NA but we do have EU region requirements later this year.
[05:17] Sofia Martinez: We offer regional routing and private deployments in EU regions; we'll note that in the security doc.
[05:22] [05:20] Mike Chen: Quick question 
 LLM model variants: is Redwood providing model catalog and quantized variants?
[05:26] Jamie Park: Yes, we maintain a model catalog with curated open models and our performance profiles. We also provide quantized variants and smaller specialized models for low-latency use cases.
[05:34] [06:00] Priya Rao: About benchmark metrics 
 can the script output token-level breakdown and GPU utilization?
[05:39] Sofia Martinez: Yes, the repo includes perf dashboards with token/sec, GPU utilization, CPU, memory, and GPU kernel timings when available. For private/Dedicated we'll collect nvprof/metrics where allowed.
[05:50] Mike Chen: For streaming, how do you measure time-to-first-token? We need under 100ms ideally for first token on short responses.
[05:56] Sofia Martinez: We measure time-to-first-byte at the client and isolate model first-token time. 100ms is aggressive but achievable for small models on Dedicated; network RTT can be a big part of that.
[06:06] [06:20] Jamie Park: We should capture your baseline network RTT between your client region and Redwood region 
 Priya can collaborate with our infra team during the run.
[06:13] Priya Rao: I'll provide test locations and internal network metrics.
[06:16] [06:35] Mike Chen: Any examples of customers hitting similar targets?
[06:19] Jamie Park: Yes 
 a payments customer (redacted) achieved p95 180ms on Dedicated for 50-200 concurrency with KV cache and smaller model variant; we ran the same workload against Hosted and saw similar median but more p95 variance during spikes.
[06:30] Sofia Martinez: We can share anonymized benchmark spreadsheets 
 I'll attach them.
[06:36] [06:44] Daniel Ortiz: What about fallback policies if the main model gets overloaded?
[06:40] Sofia Martinez: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to lighter model variants or different regions. You can set policies: prefer low-latency, or prefer low-cost. We'll help design based on your SLA.
[06:51] Mike Chen: Good. For our PoC, timeline is two to four weeks ideally. We want hosted smoke in week 1, dedicated benchmark in week 2, and decision by week 4.
[06:59] Jamie Park: That timeline is reasonable. We'll align resources.
[07:03] [07:10] Priya Rao: Are there any known transcription issues in your docs? (laughs)
[07:07] Jamie Park: (laugh) yes sometimes our automatic notes swap model names, but we'll send crisp docs.
[07:12] Sofia Martinez: Action checklist: we'll send benchmark repo, pricing, security pack, and propose times for the workload run.
[07:20] [07:35] Mike Chen: One more thing 
 how do you account for batching delays in load gen? If generator batches client requests, that hides real client latency.
[07:26] Sofia Martinez: Our generator simulates arrival patterns and measures per-request latency before batching. We can configure Poisson arrival or your real arrival trace to make it realistic.
[07:36] Daniel Ortiz: Excellent. Any blockers to run a hosted smoke right away?
[07:41] Jamie Park: Just sample prompts and an email to set the trial project 
 we'll provision a sandbox workspace.
[07:44] Priya Rao: I'll send sample traces and auth contacts after the call.
[07:47] [08:00] Mike Chen: Ok that's it from me 
 thanks for the clarity.
[07:52] Jamie Park: Great 
 recap and next steps: Jamie sends pricing and Dedicated sizing; Sofia shares benchmark scripts and perf runbook; Mike sends sample prompts and QPS profile. We'll schedule the benchmark next week.
[07:59] Sofia Martinez: Sending the links, and I'll cc infra.
[08:03] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[08:05] Jamie Park: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cachee" or "Redwood Dedicate"), filler words, and minor speaker attribution noise. Benchmark plan: run Hosted smoke -> collect p50/p95/p99 -> run Dedicated sizing tests at concurrencies 50/150/250 -> run streaming tests measuring time-to-first-token and tokens/sec -> analyze GPU util and kernel timings.
